study_identification_part.si4_title: Comprehensive volumetric phenotyping of the neonatal brain in Down syndrome

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction explicitly state the aim to perform normative modeling of regional neonatal brain tissue volumes using a large control cohort and to quantify deviations in DS neonates, motivated by potential early clinical utility.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "...we used a cross-sectional sample of 493 ... to perform normative modeling of regional brain tissue volumes... Deviation from the normative mean was quantified in 25 neonates with DS..."; "In this study, we aimed to conduct the first detailed regional volumetric analysis of the neonatal brain in DS. We used a robust cross-sectional sample... to perform normative modeling..."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort (dHCP) is described with inclusion/exclusion criteria, neuroradiology review for image quality, final sample size, and explicit exclusion reasons (incidental findings, low Bayley scores, repeat scans).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "A total of 493 preterm- to term-born neonates ... were selected from the dHCP ... Exclusion criteria included incidental findings on MRI ... and Bayley III ... below 70 ... No repeat scans ... Healthy neonates from twin pregnancies were included."; "All MRI scans were examined by a neonatal neuroradiologist. Exclusion criteria for the dHCP scans were incidental findings..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: The GPR normative model accounts for key covariates (sex, PMA at scan, and age from birth). Data are single-site, so site effects are not applicable.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "...accounting for sex, PMA at scan (in weeks), and age from birth (in weeks) variables."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source for the reference cohort is specified as the developing Human Connectome Project (dHCP), with website and citation.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "...were selected from the dHCP (www.developingconnectome.org) (Edwards et al. 2022)..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: The reference cohort uses an existing dataset (dHCP); per item instructions, for secondary data answer NA.

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described, including bias-field correction, brain extraction, segmentation with the dHCP structural pipeline, and QC with visual inspection and manual correction (ITK-SNAP).
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "...segmented using the dHCP structural pipeline (https://github.com/BioMedIA/dhcp-structural-pipeline)... Tissue segments for all DS and control scans were visually inspected for accuracy ... any mislabelled voxels were manually corrected using ITK-SNAP (version 3.8.0)."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No internal data partitioning (e.g., cross-validation or hold-out) is reported for the reference cohort; the model is described as fit on the control sample and then used to extract z-scores for DS.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Gaussian process regression (GPR) was used to model ... in the control sample ... Subsequently, the GPR model was used to extract ... z-scores ... for an independent sample of 25 neonates with DS..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative model is applied to the DS clinical cohort; there is no application to an independent external healthy dataset.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "...used to extract individualized ... z-scores ... for an independent sample of 25 neonates with DS..."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical model (Gaussian process regression) and software (GPy in Python) are specified, but key model settings (e.g., kernel type, priors) are not detailed.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "GPR modeling was implemented using GPy in Python ..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: No quantitative model performance metrics (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, interval coverage) are reported for the normative model on the reference cohort.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: Methods describe GPR modeling and downstream analyses of z-scores, but do not report fit/calibration metrics for the reference model.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning was performed; per item guidance, if no partitioning, answer NA.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: The paper specifies software and some versions (R, GraphPad Prism, ITK-SNAP, R packages), links the dHCP structural pipeline and GPy, and states data availability (dHCP open-release; eBiDS upon request). Code or trained models are not provided.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "...segmented using the dHCP structural pipeline (https://github.com/BioMedIA/dhcp-structural-pipeline)..."; "GPR modeling was implemented using GPy in Python..."; "All analyses ... GraphPad Prism v9.1.1 or R v4.1.0..."; "The dHCP is an open-access project... Data from the eBiDS study are available ... upon reasonable request."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Eligibility and diagnostic confirmation (postnatal karyotype) are provided; image quality review by neuroradiologist is described; final sample size and exclusion reasons are reported.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS ... A total of 36 neonates ... Ten ... excluded ... due to ... old acquisition protocols ... One ... excluded ... due to an acute brain infarction... Therefore, data from 25 neonates with DS ... were used..."; "All MRI scans were examined by a neonatal neuroradiologist..."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses incorporate clinical covariates beyond demographics, including congenital heart defect status (CHD+ vs CHD-).
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "For neonates with DS, CHD diagnosis (n=13, 52% of DS group)..."; "...to test statistical difference between groups, including DS vs control, or DS neonates with CHD vs without CHD."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: The clinical cohort data source is described (recruited at St Thomas' Hospital, London) with a clear collection period (2014–2021).
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited ... at St Thomas' Hospital London ... A total of 36 neonates ... between 2014 and 2021."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample size and demographics are reported; clinical characteristics such as CHD and additional comorbidities are documented (with details in Supplementary Tables).
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "...data from 25 neonates with DS [12 female, 10 preterm births < 37 weeks GA, PMA at scan median (range) = 40.57 (32.43-45.57) weeks] (Table S1)..."; "For neonates with DS, CHD diagnosis (n=13, 52% of DS group) and details of additional clinical comorbidities can be found in Supplementary Tables S2 and S3..."; "Demographic information for the DS (n=25, 48.0% female) ... summarized in Table 2."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Diagnostic confirmation for DS is described (postnatal karyotype). No structured symptom scales are applicable/reported for neonates in this study.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "Neonates with a postnatally confirmed karyotype for DS were recruited..."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The paper explains z-scores as deviations normalized by predictive uncertainty, defines quantitative thresholds for extreme deviations (|z| ≥ 2.6), and discusses potential clinical implications at a high level. Directionality is implicit rather than explicitly defined for each region.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "The difference between predicted and observed values, normalized by the predictive confidence ... represents the deviation ... expressed as a z-score ..."; "Extreme deviations in volume were taken as a z-score ≤ -2.6 or ≥ +2.6 SD..."; "...the ability to assess phenotypic severity at the neonatal stage may help guide early interventions..."
